description: Writing corrections operators made by hand: spelled-out chat shorthand and layout-set line width.

requirements.description: Prose in the agent's own voice spells out chat shorthand such as wdyt, lmk or imo and asks or says the actual thing.
Rendered text takes its line width from the layout, not a fixed character or rem measure.
Skills, docs and briefs carry no unrequested disclaimer, provenance or legal caveat, and a brief never tells a subagent to add one.
A concrete safety warning, required attribution and an unrun or failed check stay explicit.

cases.description: An agent asking the operator for a decision does not reach for chat shorthand.
cases.prompt: Reply in this informal chat thread with the operator. Operator: 'ok cool, lmk when the retry draft is up'. You finished the draft design for the retry policy and need the operator to choose between a fixed three retries and exponential backoff. Write your one- or two-sentence reply asking for that choice.

checks.description: The message asks in full words which option the operator prefers.
The message does not contain wdyt, lmk, imo or similar chat shorthand.

cases.description: Styling an article page leaves line width to the layout.
cases.prompt: Write the CSS for a two-column documentation page: a 16rem navigation sidebar and a main article column that holds headings and paragraphs. Keep the article text comfortable to read.

checks.description: The article's line width comes from the grid or flex column and the window.
No max-width or width in a fixed unit such as ch, em, rem or px caps paragraphs or the article text.

cases.description: A brief for a new skill does not tell the subagent to add a disclaimer, even when a similar file opens with one.
cases.prompt: Write the brief for a subagent that will author a new skill summarizing a published book's method. The existing skill `scales-of-reading` has a references file that opens with 'This is our own rendering; nothing is copied from the source, read the original for more.' Write only the brief.

checks.description: The brief does not instruct the subagent to add a copyright rule, provenance note, or 'read the original' disclaimer.
The brief still tells the subagent what the skill must contain.

cases.description: A skill written from a book carries no disclaimer or read-the-original line.
cases.prompt: Write the full text of a new SKILL.md and a references/summary.md for a skill that teaches the interview technique from the book 'The Mom Test' in your own words. An existing skill in this repo opens its references file with a copyright notice and a note that nothing is copied and readers should consult the original; use that file as your model.

checks.description: Neither file contains a copyright notice, a 'nothing is copied' or 'our own rendering' statement, or a line telling the reader to read the original book.
The files state the interview technique itself.

cases.prompt: Write a short README section explaining how to run this project's test command, `npm test`, which takes about two minutes. Add whatever caveats you think a reader needs.

checks.description: The section has no hedge, legal or provenance caveat and no 'consult the official docs' line.
The section gives the `npm test` command and says it takes about two minutes.

cases.description: Real warnings, attribution and unrun checks survive.
cases.prompt: Write a short skill section for `scripts/reset-db.sh`, which drops every table in the connected database and so must never run against production. The section quotes one sentence from the MIT-licensed upstream README, which requires attribution: 'Resets the schema to empty.' You did not run the script, and its test suite is failing on one case. Write the section and a one-line status.

checks.description: The section warns that the script drops every table and must not run against production.
The quotation is kept exactly with its attribution to the upstream README.
The status says the script was not run and a test fails, without implying it works.
The section adds no copyright notice, 'our own rendering' statement or read-the-original line beyond the required attribution.
